comment: One mechanism per gate. `check` is a rule the shipped runner evaluates against the repository; `files` are the config fragments the runner cannot replace (a real linter's config, a policy, a mutation config). A gate with no machine check still gets an attestation file, because a gate nobody records is a gate nobody meets. Each rule also names the milestone (`phase`, 0-5) at which it becomes blocking: a gate that cannot be met yet is sequenced, not waived, so a fresh repository is not 20 failures on day one.

G0-RUN.how: The README contains a fenced command block a new contributor can copy.
G0-RUN.mechanism: The README itself. This check only proves a command is written down; G0-SMOKE proves it works.

G0-CHECK.how: A CI workflow runs a lint or typecheck step on pull requests.
G0-CHECK.mechanism: The workflow file. Add the same command to the README so a local run matches CI.

G0-SMOKE.how: A smoke or end-to-end test file exists for the primary journey.
G0-SMOKE.mechanism: One end-to-end test, exercising the documented interface rather than the internals.

G1-CI.how: A CI workflow runs the test command.
G1-CI.mechanism: The workflow file, plus a branch protection rule that makes the job required. The rule is in the forge, not in the repository.

G1-DOMAIN-TESTS.how: Every core requirement carries an @req anchor in a test file.
G1-DOMAIN-TESTS.mechanism: `spec-check.mjs` counts the anchors; this gate fails while a core requirement has none.

G1-AC-TRACE.how: Every requirement marked automated has a test anchor.

G1-RUNBOOK.how: The README covers running, testing and deploying.
G1-RUNBOOK.mechanism: Three headings. A runbook with none of them is a README for the author.

G1-SECRETS.how: No credential-shaped string is committed, and a gitleaks config is present for the pre-commit hook.
G1-SECRETS.mechanism: The runner scans the working tree; gitleaks scans history. Both are needed: this file cannot see what was already committed and deleted.

G2-AUTHZ.how: A denial-path test exists, and the authorization policy has a home outside the handlers.
G2-AUTHZ.mechanism: The rego policy is evaluated with `conftest test --policy enforcement/policy`; the runner only proves a denial test exists.

G2-THREAT.how: A threat model lists accepted risks, each with an owner.
G2-THREAT.mechanism: The document. A threat model without an owner column is a list of worries.

G2-CONTRACTS.how: A machine-readable contract or contract test exists in the repository.
G2-CONTRACTS.mechanism: The skeleton consumes a recorded fixture; replace the fixture with a real capture, not a mock written from the docs.

G2-OBSERVABILITY.how: Source code propagates a correlation or request id.
G2-OBSERVABILITY.mechanism: A grep is the weakest form of this check. It proves the identifier exists, not that every path carries it.

G2-MIGRATIONS.how: Schema changes live as migrations in version control.
G2-MIGRATIONS.mechanism: The migration directory. Forward-only is a convention the runner cannot see; the restore drill in G3-RESTORE is what proves it.

G2-ADR.how: At least one ADR records a decision and its consequence.
G2-ADR.mechanism: The ADR directory. An ADR with no consequence section is a changelog entry.

G2-DRIFT.how: `spec-check.mjs --repo .` passes: every anchor resolves and every done requirement is proven.
G2-DRIFT.mechanism: `spec-check.mjs`, shipped with the packet. This gate is the one check that needs no project code to be honest.

G3-MUTATION.how: A mutation configuration and a separate semantic-oracle manifest bind every automated requirement to a black-box or property test outside its ordinary unit test file.
G3-MUTATION.mechanism: The runner rejects an absent/malformed manifest, a missing requirement oracle, or an oracle with no @req anchor/assertion. CI must run the selected mutation tool; the structural runner cannot measure its score or prove the oracle is complete.

G3-PROPERTY.how: A property-based testing library is present and used by a test.
G3-PROPERTY.mechanism: The generated-seed corpus is not checked; a property test without a recorded seed is an example test in disguise.

G3-SLO.how: An SLO document states a target percentage and an error budget.
G3-SLO.mechanism: The document plus the alert rule. The number is a policy decision; this check only proves someone wrote it down.

G3-RESTORE.how: A restore drill is recorded with a date, what was restored and who verified it.
G3-RESTORE.mechanism: An attestation, because the drill happens against production data the repository cannot see.

G3-SECURITY.how: The threat model records a per-release review.
G3-SECURITY.mechanism: The document plus the security regression suite. A review nobody signed for is a meeting.

G3-ROLLBACK.how: A rollback or kill switch has been executed once, and the record says when.
G3-ROLLBACK.mechanism: An attestation, because executing the rollback is the evidence. An unexecuted rollback procedure is a paragraph.

G1-INCIDENT.how: docs/runbook.md names an owner, an escalation channel and first-response steps.
G1-INCIDENT.mechanism: The runbook file. This proves the fields are present, not that the named person knows the product; the three diagnostic steps are the part to read.

G2-CONSENT.how: docs/consent-basis.md records a lawful basis, a withdrawal path and a retention period.
G2-CONSENT.mechanism: The document. It cannot tell whether the basis is the right one — that is a legal judgement, and the reviewer's, not the runner's.

G2-REVIEW.how: docs/review-record.md carries at least one row with a date, an author and a different reviewer.
G2-REVIEW.mechanism: The record. A table you fill in alone proves nothing; the gate is the habit of opening it.

G3-PHI-ENCRYPT.how: docs/phi-encryption.md names every PHI store with its transit and rest encryption and a rotation interval.
G3-PHI-ENCRYPT.mechanism: The attestation. It records an owner's claim per store; it cannot show that a field is unreadable in raw storage, which is what the requirement's test must prove.

G3-AUDIT-RETENTION.how: docs/audit-retention.md names the audit destination, its append-only mechanism, the retention period and the restore path.
G3-AUDIT-RETENTION.mechanism: The document. A retention period that exists only in a table row is a policy, not a proven control.

G3-SUBJECT-RIGHTS.how: A test exercises both the subject-access export and the erasure path.
G3-SUBJECT-RIGHTS.mechanism: The test names. It cannot show the export covers every store the product owns — that is the requirement's checklist.

G3-CARD-SCOPE.how: A test asserts that a card-shaped value is rejected or absent from storage and logs.
G3-CARD-SCOPE.mechanism: One test. It cannot prove no future endpoint accepts one; the review of the payment surface is the compensating control.
